mentions.name: Kantoku kanji recognition prototype
mentions.description: This open source, open weight supervised learning model recognizes Japanese kanji characters drawn on screen. The prototype is written in Julia using a simple neural network; because input is in vector format, the convolution layer is swapped for a path simplification algorithm, which reached 100% accuracy on a small test set with only ~20 samples per character after 30 training iterations. Further experiments with the prototype are planned before release.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I just started on an open source and open weight supervised learning model to recognize japanese kanji characters drawn on the screen.

I have a working prototype written in Julia which is a very simple neural network.

mentions.name: Kantoku prototype (handwritten kanji recognition model)
mentions.description: An open source, open weight supervised learning model that recognizes Japanese kanji characters drawn on screen. The working prototype is a simple neural network written in Julia that takes vector-format stroke input, replacing the convolution layer with a path simplification algorithm; with about 20 samples per character it reached 100% accuracy on a small test set after 30 training iterations.
mentions.problem: Traditional convolutional neural networks don't work out of the box on vector-format input.
